# `owner-link` commands

## `owner-link`

Make a fresh one-time link for the owner (this computer's login) to choose their password in the browser, as `setup` does: it works once, expires (two hours by default) and replaces any earlier link. It never resets a password: once the owner has one, it is refused. Use it instead of rerunning setup when a link expired or was lost.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | hub |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | the local operating-system login, which must be the installation's owner |
| Capability | init |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | Local only; no HTTP route. |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow owner-link --json`

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bind` | `--bind` | string | no | no | "127.0.0.1:8765" | Address the host listens on, host:port (loopback); the link opens there; maximum length 128 |
| `link_minutes` | `--link-minutes` | integer | no | no | 120 | Minutes the link stays valid; minimum 1; maximum 1440 |
| `public_origin` | `--public-origin` | string \| null | no | yes | null | The https://host[:port] a TLS proxy in front of the host serves (for example what `colony serve` prints); the links and the MCP configuration use it. Defaults to [host] public_origin in config.toml |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |

### HTTP

This command has no HTTP route.

### Output

| JSON field | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `url` | string | yes | no | — | The one-time link; it works once and only for a person with no password yet |
| `expires_at` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `host_running` | boolean | yes | no | — | Whether the host answers at the link's address now; start it with `bookflow serve --background` |
| `content` | string | yes | no | — | — |
| `media_type` | string | no | no | "text/plain" | — |

Example JSON output:

```json
{
  "content": "value",
  "expires_at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "host_running": false,
  "media_type": "text/plain",
  "url": "value",
  "username": "value"
}
```

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|

| `E_COMPANY_NOT_FOUND` | No such company. |

| `E_FS_UNKNOWN` | The filesystem type of the path could not be determined. |
| `E_GUARD_REFUSED` | Bookflow's own safety check in the database refused this write, so nothing was saved. This is a Bookflow bug, not a problem with your input or your disk: please report it with this error's details and request id. |
| `E_INTERNAL` | Internal failure. |
| `E_IO` | A filesystem operation failed. |
| `E_MIGRATION_FAILED` | A schema migration failed; the database was backed up first and is unchanged. |
| `E_NETWORK_NOT_ALLOWED` | Binding outside loopback needs --allow-network. |

| `E_PARTIAL_WRITE` | The authoritative write committed, but a secondary update remains incomplete. |
| `E_PERMISSION` | The acting user may not run this command here. |

| `E_SCHEMA_BEHIND` | The database schema is behind this version of Bookflow; run `bookflow upgrade`. |
| `E_SCHEMA_UNKNOWN` | The database schema revision is not known to this version of Bookflow; upgrade Bookflow. |
